q: how many reps should i do
how many sets and reps should i do
how many reps for strength vs muscle
a: The rep range depends on your goal, and the ranges overlap more than gym lore suggests: (1) Strength: 1-5 reps per set with heavy weight (85-100% of your one-rep max), long rests (3-5 min). (2) Muscle growth (hypertrophy): 6-12 reps at moderate weight (65-85% of 1RM), 60-90 second rests — the classic sweet spot. (3) Endurance: 15+ reps with lighter weight, short rests. The practical truth: research shows muscle growth happens across the whole 5-30 rep range as long as you take each set close to failure (leaving 0-3 reps in reserve). So pick a rep range you enjoy, focus on effort and form, and progress the weight over time. A standard beginner program is 3-4 sets of 8-12 reps per exercise, 2-4 times per week. The most important variables are consistency and progressive overload (adding weight or reps over time) — not the exact rep count.

q: how to get rid of belly fat
how to lose stubborn stomach fat
how to reduce belly fat fast
a: The short answer: you can't target belly fat — 'spot reduction' doesn't work, and there's no food or exercise that selectively burns belly fat. Belly fat comes off when overall body fat comes down, through a calorie deficit (eat slightly fewer calories than you burn) sustained over time. The fastest reliable approach: (1) Create a modest deficit (300-500 calories/day) — cutting sugary drinks and ultra-processed foods is the easiest lever. (2) Prioritize protein and fiber, which keep you full. (3) Strength train — building muscle raises your resting metabolism and improves body composition. (4) Do some cardio you'll stick with (walking, running, cycling); intensity matters less than consistency. (5) Sleep 7-9 hours — poor sleep raises cortisol and hunger hormones and is strongly linked to belly fat gain. (6) Manage stress — chronic stress raises cortisol, which promotes abdominal fat storage. Expect realistic progress: 0.5-1 kg (1-2 lb) per week of total fat loss, and belly fat is typically among the last places to go. Ab exercises build the muscle underneath but don't remove the fat covering it.

q: how to calculate a calorie deficit
how many calories should i eat to lose weight
a: A calorie deficit simply means eating fewer calories than your body burns, which forces it to use stored fat for energy — that's what drives weight loss. Your total daily burn is your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR — what you burn at rest) plus activity; you can estimate it with online TDEE calculators (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) that factor in age, sex, weight, height, and activity level. To lose weight, eat roughly 300-500 calories below your TDEE per day, which yields about 0.5 kg (1 lb) per week — a pound of fat is ~3,500 calories. Faster deficits (1000+ under) cause more muscle loss, hunger, and are hard to sustain. Key points: (1) A deficit is easier to maintain with high-protein, high-fiber foods that keep you full. (2) The scale fluctuates daily with water and food — judge trends over weeks, not days. (3) As you lose weight, your TDEE drops (less body to move), so you may need to eat less or move more to keep losing. (4) Never go below roughly 1,200 calories (women) / 1,500 (men) without medical supervision. For most people, a modest deficit plus walking and strength training is the sustainable path.
